sentiment.rationale: The document reports a clean beat and raise: Q4 revenue of $10.3B beat the roughly $9.7B consensus, and Q1 2026 revenue guidance of ~$9.8B is ahead of the ~$9.4B consensus. Management explicitly states 'significant top and bottom line growth in 2026' and reaffirms a path to >35% CAGR over 3-5 years. The only material risks are China GPU uncertainty and a semi-custom gaming decline, but these are secondary to the strong forward guidance.

summary.revenue: Q4 revenue $10.3B, up 34% year over year and 11% sequentially. Full-year revenue $34.6B, up 34%.
summary.eps: Q4 diluted EPS $1.53, up 40% year over year. Full-year EPS $4.17, up 26%.
summary.guidance: Q1 2026 revenue guided to approximately $9.8B plus or minus $300M, ahead of the roughly $9.4B consensus. Management expects 'significant top and bottom line growth in 2026' and reaffirms a path to >35% CAGR over 3-5 years.
summary.margin: Q4 gross margin 57%, up 290 basis points year over year. Excluding a $306M inventory reserve release and China MI308 revenue, gross margin would have been approximately 55%, up 80 bps year over year. Q1 2026 gross margin guided to approximately 55%.
key_risks: China GPU sales are highly uncertain; only $100M assumed in Q1 guide and no additional revenue forecasted.
Semi-custom gaming revenue expected to decline a significant double-digit percentage in 2026.
PC headwinds from memory and component inflation, with the second half modeled subseasonal.
key_opportunities: Data center AI business accelerating with MI350 series ramp and MI450/Helios inflection in second half 2026.
Server CPU demand surging, with EPYC order book strengthening and Q1 server CPU revenue expected to grow sequentially despite seasonal decline.
Client business growing via enterprise share gains and premium product mix.
Embedded segment returning to growth with record design wins ($17B in 2025).

management_tone.label: confident
management_tone.justification: Management uses phrases like '2025 was a defining year,' 'we are entering a multiyear demand super cycle,' and 'we see a clear path to achieve the ambitious targets,' indicating strong conviction in the forward outlook.

evidence.claim: Q4 revenue was $10.3B, up 34% year over year.
evidence.quote: fourth quarter revenue grew 34% year over year to $10.3 billion led by record EPYC, Ryzen, and Instinct processor sales.

evidence.claim: Q4 diluted EPS was $1.53, up 40% year over year.
evidence.quote: diluted earnings per share was a record $1.53, an increase of 40% year over year.

evidence.claim: Q1 2026 revenue guidance of ~$9.8B is ahead of the ~$9.4B consensus.
evidence.quote: We expect revenue to be approximately $9.8 billion plus or minus $300 million including approximately $100 million of MI308 sales to China. At the midpoint of our guidance, revenue is expected to be up 32% year over year... ahead of the roughly $9.4B consensus

evidence.claim: Management expects significant top and bottom line growth in 2026.
evidence.quote: we expect significant top-line and bottom-line growth in 2026, led by increased adoption of EPYC and Instinct, continued client share gains, and a return to growth in our Embedded segment.

evidence.claim: Q4 gross margin was 57%, up 290 bps year over year.
evidence.quote: Gross margin was 57%, up 290 basis points year over year.

evidence.claim: China GPU sales are highly uncertain; only $100M assumed in Q1 guide.
evidence.quote: We are not forecasting any additional revenue from China just because it's a very dynamic situation... we thought it prudent, not to forecast any additional revenue other than the $100 million that we called out.

evidence.claim: Semi-custom gaming revenue expected to decline a significant double-digit percentage in 2026.
evidence.quote: For 2026, we expect semi-custom SoC annual revenue to decline by a significant double-digit percentage as we enter the seventh year of what has been a very strong console cycle.

evidence.claim: PC headwinds from memory and component inflation, with second half modeled subseasonal.
evidence.quote: we're probably seeing the PC TAM down a bit just given some of the inflationary pressures of the commodities pricing, including memory. The way we are modeling the year is, let's call it, second half a bit subseasonal to first half.

evidence.claim: Data center AI business accelerating with MI350 ramp and MI450 inflection.
evidence.quote: our AI business is accelerating. With the launch of MI400 series and Helios representing a major inflection point for the business as we deliver leadership performance and TCO at the chip, compute tray, and rack level.

evidence.claim: Server CPU demand surging, with Q1 server CPU revenue expected to grow sequentially.
evidence.quote: we see server CPU growing from Q4 into Q1 in what normally is seasonally down. And that continues throughout the year.

evidence.claim: Embedded segment returning to growth with record design wins.
evidence.quote: We closed $17 billion in design wins in 2025, up nearly 20% year over year as we now won more than $50 billion of embedded designs since acquiring Xilinx.
2025 was a defining year for Advanced Micro Devices, Inc. With record revenue, net income, and free cash flow driven by broad-based demand for our high-performance computing and AI products.

review_flags.reason: The sentiment score of 0.75 is based on the guidance raise and strong forward language, but the document also notes that the Q4 beat included a $306M inventory reserve release and $390M in China MI308 revenue that were not in guidance. The score may be slightly elevated if these one-time items are considered non-recurring. A human reviewer should assess whether the organic beat is as strong as the headline suggests.
